A.explanation: Fringe separation follows $x = \lambda D/a$, so $x$ is proportional to $1/a$ and falls steeply at small $a$ then flattens.

B.explanation: This shows $x$ increasing with $a$, which contradicts $x = \lambda D/a$ where larger slit separation gives closer fringes.

C.explanation: This shows $x$ falling to zero at a finite $a$ like a quarter-circle, whereas $1/a$ only approaches zero as $a$ becomes very large.

D.explanation: This shows $x$ increasing with $a$ with decreasing gradient, whereas the physics requires $x$ to decrease when $a$ increases.

hints: Notice the wavelength $\lambda$ and the slit-to-screen distance $D$ are fixed, so only the slit separation $a$ changes the fringe separation $x$.
Connect this to the two-source fringe formula $x = \lambda D/a$, so $x$ is inversely proportional to $a$.
Think what the curve $y = 1/a$ looks like: very large when $a$ is near zero and approaching zero as $a$ grows, with no intercept on the $a$-axis.
walkthrough: Identify the fixed quantities from the diagram and text: single wavelength $\lambda$ and fixed slit-to-screen distance $D$, with variable slit separation $a$ and observed fringe separation $x$.
State the governing two-slit interference rule: $x = \lambda D/a$, where $\lambda D$ is constant here.
Rewrite as $x \propto 1/a$, so doubling $a$ halves $x$ and halving $a$ doubles $x$.
Sketch the implication: as $a \to 0$, $x$ becomes very large, and as $a$ becomes large, $x$ tends toward zero without cutting the $a$-axis.
Match this decreasing reciprocal curve to the graphs: only the curve that starts high on the $x$-axis and falls with decreasing gradient fits. This is option A.
